skill_entry.name: 13. A number in production code carries its role: a name in reach, a derivation, or the stem alone (the suffix convention stays inside the author's kernel files)
skill_entry.trigger: In h/ or src/, never t/, any one: (A) an added production line, or an unchanged line of a function the diff changes by more than a rename, uses a numeric literal other than 0 and 1 in arithmetic, an index, a comparison, a shift, a mask, an array dimension, a capacity argument or a plain argument, and no comment on that line or the line above names what it measures; an unchanged line counts only when the diff changes, or a hunk contains, the definition of the constant that would replace the literal (2948416014, 3350031805). (B) A removed line names a constexpr or macro and the added line in the same hunk spells that slot as a literal, a sizeof or an expression (2915275194). (C) The diff changes a named constant's value and a message in a file that uses it still prints the old value (3350031805). (D) A new sizing constant, or an added allocation or address formula that multiplies by one, has no derivation (3350173837, 2947992404). (E) A count constant is returned as a failure value (3235796275). (F) The diff adds or renames a value-suffixed constant; report the stem, never the suffix.
skill_entry.procedure: Scan added lines, comments and strings stripped, for literals of 2 or more and hex literals; drop a literal the paired removed line already carried. Scan the whole body of a touched function only where the hunk adds or removes a statement; keep an unchanged-line literal only when a same-value name is defined in the same file or h/pos/config.hpp and the diff changes that definition or a hunk contains it. Per literal, look up a constexpr or #define of the same value (or value plus one for a last-index comparison) whose name states the same quantity; prefer the name the file already pairs with the other operand. With no name: sibling operand named, an explanation of an equal literal removed in the hunk, count the file's bare literals, name the config file. Pair removed names with added literals (equal value: merge artifact?). For changed constants, grep the old value in messages that print its quantity. For sizing constants: derivation, sibling limits, use sites, whether a test can shrink it. Sentinel: point at INVALID_*. Suffixed: existing stem procedure.
skill_entry.question: Can a reader at this line say what the number measures without asking the author, either from a name that already exists in reach, from a comment that derives it, or from the stem of the constant alone; and if a name used to stand in this slot, why did it leave?
skill_entry.do_not_fire: Literals 0 and 1 and the guide's exceptions (zero init, reset, comparison, empty value with the parameter name visible; a one-use alignas). A literal 2 in a pair or halving role (`num_fetchers / 2`, `pdci < 2` drew nothing in 2789750267) unless the hunk removes the comment that explained an equal literal (3454926024); a commented `/ 2` elsewhere in the file does not count. Any literal in t/. A lane width, shift amount or packing factor in SIMD or kernel code (no corpus row). A literal that only bounds or formats diagnostic output; inside a debug-gated block fire only when an existing name stands in reach (2737603648). A literal in a log string that is the claim itself. A literal an adjacent comment marks temporary. A value-suffixed name inside the author's own kernel files (6021333114). A stem that names a role (`BF16_BITS_16`); namings of 1, true, false. An author's written deferral: nit, never block. A message mismatch unrelated to a changed constant, a missing comment on an env default, and placement belong to other checks.
skill_entry.finding_shape: (A), (D), (E): "`<expression>` (<file:line>) uses the hard-coded <N>; <config file:line> already names that quantity `<name>` [| nothing in h/ names it, and the file has <k> more bare literals (<list>)]. Should we use `<name>` here rather than <N> [| name it next to `<siblings>` in <config file>, or add a comment saying what <N> measures]? Nit." (D) sizing: "where did <N> come from? <sibling limit> is <M> on the <other> side; is <new constant> meant to be independent of it? Could <class> take the size as a constructor argument defaulting to <new constant>, so tests can reach wrap-around and full with a small queue?" (B), (C): "why replace `<name>` with hard-coded `<N>`? They are the same value, so <bound> is unchanged; merge artifact? [| the value changed from <old> to <N>: was this intentional? If so, a comment or a named constant for <N>.]" (F): the existing stem shape, unchanged.
skill_entry.severity_wade_uses: Nit for an existing-name substitution, a sentinel or a shape comment: `just a nit, but returning `NUM_CLASSES` as an *error* condition seems non-intuitive` (3235796275), `can we add a short comment explaining the `/ 2` above?` (3454926024), a ```suggestion block when the fix is one line (2737603648, 2789750267, 3350031805). Minor question for a name that became a literal: `why replace `tron::hardware::hwkv_max_layers` with hard-coded `32`?` (2915275194), `was this intentional? If so, should probably note what's special about `1000`` (3307459854), `why 64? perhaps a comment explaining...` (3120756577). Normal, as a design question with two readings, for a sizing constant with no derivation (`Are you intentionally decoupling TX from RX here?`, 3350173837) or a constant that fixes a model parameter (ending `Right?`, 2947992404). General statements are filed as clean-up remarks with a smiley: `I really don't like all these magic numbers we use everywhere ;)` (2636393495), `We really should try to use some constexpr values or something... instead of these magic numbers :-)` (2915246595). On a merge or port PR, report no-name findings as one such remark, not per line. Never blocking: he approved PR 1666 eight minutes after the comment (2620219338 at 17:15:25Z, APPROVED 17:23:55Z, before the author replied at 18:05:31Z) and PR 1730 seven minutes after (2636393495 at 21:48:02Z, APPROVED 21:55:36Z, no author reply in the corpus).
skill_entry.evidence_scope: hunk; full file (the whole touched function at HEAD where a statement was added or removed, because two rows sit on unchanged lines; the removed comment lines of the hunk; the file's other bare literals; the file's own constants, since the 2948416014 name lived in the same file); other files (h/pos/config.hpp and the headers the file includes, for an existing name with the same value; the partner file on the other side of the data path, for spellings; t/ for a test that reaches wrap-around with a smaller size); commits (`git log -m -S` for the merge that kept a branch's literal; the non-merge commit that wrote it). PR body or title to detect a merge or port PR and a stated reason to retire a constant. Runtime only as a question to the author (`How deep do we get in your tests?`). Hardware meanings (8 KV heads, 32 pseudochannels) are not in the repository: the agent asks what the literal measures and never asserts the meaning.

final.procedure_commands:
## Check 13: a number in production code carries its role (widened 2026-10-06)

0. BASE for a merged PR or a reviewed commit older than the final head (the common setup's `merge-base HEAD origin/main` is wrong when the PR targets another branch, and `merge-base HEAD origin/<base_ref>` returns HEAD itself once the PR is merged): `MERGE=$(gh api repos/positron-ai/tron/pulls/N -q .merge_commit_sha); BASE=$(git -C WT merge-base HEAD $(git -C WT rev-parse $MERGE^1))`. Check `git -C WT diff --stat BASE HEAD | tail -1` against the PR file count on GitHub. (PR 2176: BASE 1794cdf67d for reviewed commit 9553cd0a11; 15 files.)

1. Bare literals in added production lines, comments and string contents stripped: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -E '^\+' | grep -vE '^\+\+\+' | sed -E 's#/\*.*\*/##g; s#//.*$##; s#"([^"\\]|\\.)*"#""#g' | grep -vE '^\+[[:space:]]*(#|\*|/\*)' | grep -nE '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_.])([2-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)([^A-Za-z0-9_.]|$)|0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+'`. Map each hit to HEAD file:line through the `@@` headers. Paired removed line: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- FILE | grep -B1 -F '<added line>'`; drop the literal when the `-` line directly above carries the same literal (a line that changed only another token keeps its old literals out: the `4` in `4 * n_kvheads * head_size * sizeof(bf16)` at src/pos/hwattention.cpp:51, PR 2176). Drop a literal when the line, the line above, or the only other use of the same literal in the same file carries a comment naming what it measures; keep it for step 3 anyway when a same-value name is reachable (2789750267 fired on `pdc == 31` under a comment). Literals inside a multi-line block comment or an `#if 0` block survive the sed and must be dropped by hand.

2. Unchanged lines of touched functions, only for hunks that add or remove a statement (never rename-only or signature-only hunks: tron-3756, 36 files, approved silently). Hunk starts at HEAD: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | awk '/^\+\+\+ /{f=substr($2,3)} /^@@/{split($3,a,/[,+]/); print f" "a[2]}' | sort -u`. Enclosing function for FILE L: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | awk -v L=L 'NR<=L && /^[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z_][^;=]*\)[[:space:]]*(const|noexcept|override)?[[:space:]]*\{[[:space:]]*$/ && !/^[[:space:]]*(if|for|while|switch)\b/ {s=NR; ind=match($0,/[^ ]/)-1} NR>L && s && !e && match($0,/[^ ]/)-1==ind && /^[[:space:]]*\}/ {e=NR} END{print s, e}'` (do not rely on the `@@` funcname text, often `struct x {` or `public:`, nor on `git diff -W`: for 2948416014 the hunk changes lines after the function's closing brace). Scan: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 's,ep' | sed -E 's#/\*.*\*/##g; s#//.*$##; s#"([^"\\]|\\.)*"#""#g' | grep -nE '(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_.])([2-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)([^A-Za-z0-9_.]|$)|0[xX][0-9a-fA-F]+'`, HEAD line = s - 1 + printed number. Keep an unchanged-line literal only when step 3 finds a same-value name defined in FILE or h/pos/config.hpp and either the diff changes that definition (`git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h | grep -E '^[-+].*\bNAME\b'`) or the definition line sits inside a hunk as a context line (`git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- FILE | grep -nF 'NAME ='`). On PR 2176 this keeps hwattention.hpp:772 (hwkv_tok_per_page = 128 at :450 is a context line of hunk `@@ -450,98 +448,9`) and drops libpos.hpp:308, self_attention.hpp:536, worker.cpp:838, fake.cpp:94.

3. Existing name per literal LIT (never for 2): `git -C WT grep -n -E '(constexpr[^=;]*=[[:space:]]*|#define[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*[[:space:]]+)\bLIT\b' HEAD -- FILE h/pos/config.hpp`, then the same over the headers FILE includes (`git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n '#include'`, one level). Same for LIT+1 (last-index comparisons such as `== 31` against a count of 32). Drop enumeration tags (a same-stem family with values 0, 1, 2 such as `activ_type_*`, `weights_type_*`). Keep a hit only when its name or comment states the quantity the literal plays here; with two candidates take the one the file already pairs with the expression's other operand: `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n '<other operand>'` (hwkv_tok_per_page over POS_PER_PAGE, because :743 reads `hwkv_pchannel_page_size_B / hwkv_tok_per_page`). A hit makes the finding "use <name> rather than the hard-coded <N>".

4. No name: sibling operand `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -n 'Lp'` (one side named, the other a literal: `tok.i == TOKEN_IDX_FOR_DEBUG && layer == 0`); removed explanation `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- FILE | grep -nE '^-[[:space:]]*//'` paired with an added or unchanged line in the same hunk that carries the literal the comment explained (3454926024: the hunk deleted `we can double-buffer the activations` above `/ 2` and added `metadata_entry_count / 2` with no comment); family count `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | sed -E 's#//.*$##' | grep -cE '[^A-Za-z0-9_.](4|8|32|128)[^A-Za-z0-9_.]'`; siblings' home `git -C WT grep -n -E 'inline constexpr' HEAD -- h/pos/config.hpp | head`. The finding is "name it next to its siblings, or say in a comment what it measures". On a PR whose title or body says it merges, ports or steps a branch (`merge of`, `Step N of`, `from hwattention_sync`), report these as one clean-up remark in the 2636393495 form, not per line.

5. Name became a literal: removed project names `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -E '^-' | grep -vE '^---' | grep -oE '\b(tron|hardware|pos)::[a-z_][a-z0-9_:]*\b|\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{3,}\b' | sort -u` (never `std::` or `fmt::`); per NAME (stem after the last `::`): definition `git -C WT grep -n -E '(constexpr[^=;(]*\bSTEM\b[[:space:]]*=|#define[[:space:]]+STEM\b)' HEAD -- h` for its VALUE; slot pairing `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h src | awk -v S=STEM -v V=VALUE '/^-/ && index($0,S) {r[++n]=$0; next} /^\+/ && n {for(i=1;i<=n;i++) if ($0 ~ /sizeof\(/ || $0 ~ ("[^A-Za-z0-9_.]" V "[^A-Za-z0-9_.]")) {print r[i]; print $0; break}} !/^[-+]/ {n=0}'`. A removed name whose slot now holds another name (`hwkv_max_layers` to `gof_max_layers()`) is not a hit. Which commit: `git -C WT log --oneline -m -S'STEM' BASE..HEAD -- FILE` (without -m a merge that kept the branch side lists nothing: 0 hits on PR 2148) plus `git -C WT log --oneline -S'<added literal expression>' BASE..HEAD -- FILE`; a name at BASE, a literal from a branch commit and a merge listed `(from BASE)` = merge artifact; a non-merge commit = ask why.

6. Old value in messages: `git -C WT diff -U0 BASE HEAD -- h | grep -E '^[-+].*(constexpr|#define)[^=]*=[[:space:]]*[0-9]' | sed -E 's/^([-+]).*\b([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*)[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*([0-9][0-9a-fA-Fx]*).*/\2 \1\3/' | sort | awk '{v[$1]=v[$1] " " $2} END{for (n in v) print n v[n]}'`; keep names with a `-` and a `+` value that differ (PR 2903: `max_cmd_fifo_depth +1024 -32`; an equal re-emit such as PR 2176's 8192 is dropped). Per NAME and OLD: `git -C WT grep -n -E '"[^"]*\bOLD\b[^"]*"' HEAD -- $(git -C WT grep -l 'NAME' HEAD -- src h)`; keep only a message that prints the constant's quantity, in the same function as a use of NAME (`cmds_in_flight {} >= 32`, worker.cpp:1680); drop the defining header's other comments (config.hpp:66 belongs to max_num_fetchers), worked examples in a Note (`page A of size 64`) and another constant's value (worker.cpp:1244 `MAX_B = 32`). Remedy: a format argument that prints the constant.

7. Sizing constants and formulas: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -nE '^\+.*(reserve|resize|assign)\(([2-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)|^\+[[:space:]]*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_:<>*& ]*[[:space:]][A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(\[([2-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)\])+[[:space:]]*;|^\+.*constexpr[^=]*=[[:space:]]*[0-9]+;'` (array declarations with a literal dimension, not indexes; every integer constexpr, the reader decides from the comment whether it is a capacity, ring size, depth, page size or cap) and `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -nE '^\+.*(alloc|size|offset|addr|stride)[^;]*[*/][[:space:]]*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*(_B|_size|_pages|_per_|_depth|_ring)'` (formulas; the constant may predate the PR: gof.cpp:98, 2947992404). Derivation = the comment on the line or above (a unit restatement such as `// 8k per pseudochannel` is not one). Sibling limits `git -C WT show HEAD:h/pos/config.hpp | grep -n -E 'ring_size|depth|in_flight|entry_count'`; use sites `git -C WT grep -n 'NAME' HEAD -- h src t`; a `member{NAME}` initializer with no constructor parameter (`git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n -A6 'CLASS('`) means tests cannot shrink it; `git -C WT grep -n -i -E 'wrap|full' HEAD -- t/` for a test that reaches those paths. For a formula: enclosing function via the step-2 awk, `sed -n 's,s+6p'` for its signature; when none of n_kv_heads, head_size, n_layers appears there, ask what <N> derives from and whether it should depend on the missing parameter. Never state the hardware meaning.

8. Count as sentinel: `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD -- h src | grep -nE '^\+.*return (NUM_|MAX_|[A-Za-z_]*(_count|_COUNT|SIZE|size\(\)))|^\+.*[Ss]entinel'`; sibling form `git -C WT show HEAD:FILE | grep -n 'INVALID_'`.

9. Suffixed definitions (existing steps): `git -C WT diff BASE HEAD | grep -nE '^\+.*\b[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*_(0X[0-9A-F]+|[0-9]+|TRUE|FALSE) *= *[^=]'`; strip the suffix, group by stem per file, flag a family unless scratch rotation; duplicates via `git -C WT grep -n -E '= <value>;' HEAD -- h src` (production only). Partner spelling for a new constant outside the author's kernel directory: `git -C WT grep -n -E '<value>' HEAD -- <partner file>` (c5d44bd86f: `0xffff0000` at kv_cache.hpp:2260 as `hi_16_of_32` versus v_vnni.hpp:84), list the spellings per file, name the partner function.

10. Report file:line at HEAD, the literal or stem, the existing name or the missing derivation, the sibling form, and the ask. Nit unless a value changed silently or a sizing constant has no derivation. Expect step 2 to be the largest list; never report from it without the bound.

On PR 2176 (BASE 1794cdf67d, reviewed 9553cd0a11): step 1 lists 2 added-line hits, 0 after the paired-removed-line rule; step 2 lists 80 hunk starts, 72 literal lines, 1 kept by the bound (h/pos/hwattention.hpp:772 `(tok_idx / 128)`, 2948416014; step 3 returns metadata_entry_count config.hpp:43, POS_PER_PAGE :31, hwkv_tok_per_page :450, the tie-break picks hwkv_tok_per_page via :743); step 5 lists POS_DATA_SIZE (h/pos/regs.hpp:40 `#define POS_DATA_SIZE 2`) paired with `sizeof(bf16)` at src/pos/hwattention.cpp:22-23 and :51 (2948209837), commit 872d32da48, non-merge, so the ask is "why"; hwkv_max_layers removed 16 added 0 but the slot holds `gof_max_layers()`, no hit; step 6 lists only the unchanged 8192 re-emit, dropped; step 7 formula grep lists gof.cpp:98 `shard_hw_pages * hwkv_pchannel_page_size_B` with the shard constructor `(PosDevice* d, uint32_t base, uint32_t layers)` at :92 naming no model parameter (2947992404); steps 8 and 9: 0. On PR 2148 (BASE e2ce886cca, reviewed 4491ff73db, HEAD 8f22c93862): step 1 lists 12 hits of which Wade raised `hwkv_pchannel_total_size_B / 2048 * 32` (hwattention.hpp:520, step 3: no 2048 name, `max_num_fetchers = 32` at config.hpp:58; 2915246595) and `layer < 32` (driver.cpp:295); step 5: hwkv_max_layers removed 1 added 0, value 32 at hwattention.hpp:480, `git log -m -S` lists `2a1c9a8005 (from e2ce886cca)`, branch commit 667a2619e5 wrote `layer < 32` = merge artifact (2915275194, author confirmed in 2919704829); driver.cpp:297-299 `- 1024`, `8, 128` are under the comment `this code will go away after we verify a fixed bitfile` and drew no naming ask. At HEAD 8f22c93862 driver.cpp:295 names hwkv_max_layers again; hwattention.hpp:475 adds `hwkv_B_per_entry = 2048`, the `* 32` stayed a literal with the comment `fixed to 32` and Wade approved. On PR 2903 (reviewed 64ea13a671, HEAD b8739108f7): step 6 pairs `max_cmd_fifo_depth -32 +1024` (config.hpp:40) with the unchanged string `cmds_in_flight {} >= 32` at src/pos/worker.cpp:1680 (3350031805; HEAD prints `>= {}` with the constant); step 7 lists `inwork_ring_size = 2048` (config.hpp:88, no derivation) against rxinfo_ring_size = 512 (:37), member initializer device.hpp:265 with a six-argument constructor and no size (3350173837, the ctor-argument ask was not implemented).
